title: The Bat and the Weasels
summary: A little bat, swooping carelessly through the twilight after moths, collided with an oak branch and tumbled into the burrow of a fierce weasel. Through unexpected trial and turning point, each character learns that it is wise to adapt your position to circumstance when survival is at stake.
full_text: A little bat, swooping carelessly through the twilight after moths, collided with an oak branch and tumbled into the burrow of a fierce weasel. The weasel seized the bat in her sharp claws, hissing with triumph: "Aha! A bird! I despise all winged creatures that fly in the air and steal eggs from nests; I intend to devour you on the spot!" The nimble-witted bat squeaked in earnest protest: "A bird? Look closely at me, good madam! What feathers do I possess? I have soft fur, sharp ears, and warm mammalian blood; I am a mouse, a fellow creature of the ground!" Seeing no feathers, the weasel was convinced and released the bat into the evening air. A few nights later, the bat tumbled into the den of another weasel who harbored a deadly hatred for all mice and rodents. "At last, a plump mouse for dinner!" snarled the second predator. "A mouse?" gasped the bat with theatrical horror. "Heaven forbid! Have you ever seen a mouse with leathery wings who can soar among the stars? I am a bird of the night, a winged aeronaut!" The second weasel marveled at the wings and let him fly away unharmed. Thus, by knowing how to present different aspects of his nature according to the danger at hand, the clever bat saved his life twice in succession.
moral: It is wise to adapt your position to circumstance when survival is at stake.

quiz.question: In the fable "The Bat and the Weasels", what situation triggers the main conflict?
options: A confrontation arising from conflicting desires, needs, or natural traits
A sudden storm that drove all animals far across the open plains
A royal decree ordering all beasts to leave the countryside
A festival where the creatures exchanged gifts in harmony
quiz.hint: Recall the events that begin the story.

quiz.question: What critical action or realization changes the course of the story?
options: One character's true nature or limits are revealed through their actions
An outside judge arrives to solve the problem for both parties
Both characters agree to forget what happened and walk away
The smaller character suddenly transforms into a giant beast
quiz.hint: Think about how the conflict reaches its resolution.

quiz.question: What essential truth does "The Bat and the Weasels" teach young readers?
options: It is wise to adapt your position to circumstance when survival is at stake.
Might and physical strength always triumph over truth and wisdom
Flattery is the safest and most honest way to make lifelong friends
It is wise to pretend to be someone you are not in times of trouble
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the final moral lesson of the fable.

discussion_questions.prompt: Who are the central characters in "The Bat and the Weasels", and what was each trying to accomplish at the beginning?
Why does this fable conclude with the moral that "It is wise to adapt your position to circumstance when survival is at stake"? How do the characters' choices illustrate this?
Think of a situation at school, sports, or home where someone might face a similar dilemma. How can you apply this lesson?
Were the consequences faced by the characters fair? What alternative choice could have produced a wiser outcome?
Imagine if the characters met again one year later. How would their behavior change based on what they learned today?
